rounds.text: Univastu India Ltd is profoundly under-appreciated, trading at a modest P/E of 17.6x while demonstrating exceptional compounding across both revenue and earnings [E1, E16, E20]. Compounded sales growth has surged by 41% over three years and reached an astonishing 107% over the trailing twelve months, matched by a 52% three-year profit growth and 163% over the TTM [E16, E17, E20, E21]. This explosive fundamental momentum translates into elite capital efficiency, highlighted by an outstanding ROCE of 30.0% and an ROE of 25.4% [E12, E13], easily outstripping sector benchmarks [E10, E9]. Furthermore, intrinsic valuation models signal massive mispricing, with a discounted cash flow estimating intrinsic value at Rs 351 per share against a market price of Rs 148, leaving an exceptional 57.8% margin of safety [E45, E46]. A reverse DCF confirms the market's pessimism is detached from reality, as today's price implies a mere 6.1% earnings growth compared to the 18.0% base case assumption [E47], while the rules-based screen awards the company a high-confidence BUY score of 92 out of 100 [E65]. Finally, technical strength supports this fundamental powerhouse, with the stock trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E50, E51]. Conceded: [E62].

Univastu India Ltd carries several notable financial and structural risks that challenge its optimistic valuation narratives. Most concerningly, debtor days have more than doubled from 58.4 to 121 days [E64], directly mirroring a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.46x where profits are running far ahead of actual cash generation due to mounting receivables and accruals [E33]. Operational momentum is also showing severe cracks, evidenced by quarterly operating margins plummeting to 14% in June 2026 from 25% in the year-ago quarter—an 11 percentage point drop [E30]—while the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are officially categorized as inconsistent [E31, E32]. Furthermore, insiders are reducing their stake, with promoter holding dropping from 72.87% in December 2023 to 64.24% by July 2026 [E41]. Shareholder returns are entirely absent as the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield despite reporting repeated profits [E4, E62], and the equity trades at a lofty price-to-book multiple of 5.44x against a sector benchmark of just 1.3x [E7]. Conceded: [E64], [E30], [E41]. Despite the increase in debtor days and the drop in the single June 2026 quarterly margin, the business is compounding at an extraordinary rate with trailing twelve-month sales growth at 107% and profit growth at 163% [E17, E21]. The bear highlights the absence of a dividend [E4, E62], but those retained earnings are fuelling phenomenal capital efficiency, delivering an exceptional ROCE of 26.6% to 30.0% and an ROE up to 25.4% that far outstrip sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13]. The elevated price-to-book ratio [E7] is entirely justified by this elite profitability and top-decile relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51]. Furthermore, technical momentum remains firmly intact with the price trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50], while a reverse DCF demonstrates that the current market price assumes a modest 6.1% earnings growth against a historical baseline vastly superior to that [E47].

Conceded: [E17], [E21]. The bull leans heavily on trailing twelve-month growth figures, but these rapid gains mask severe deteriorating trends in core execution, specifically a sharp collapse in quarterly operating margin from 25% down to 14% year-over-year in June 2026 [E30] alongside an inconsistent multi-period margin trend [E31, E32]. While the bull defends the lack of dividends [E4, E62] through high returns on capital [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13], those reported profits are failing to convert into actual cash, evidenced by a dismal cash conversion ratio of 0.46x where operating cash flow accounts for only 54% of operating profit [E33, E36]. This disconnect between accounting profits and actual cash generation is further compounded by a ballooning of debtor days from 58.4 to 121 days [E64], signaling aggressive revenue recognition or severe collection frictions. The bull dismisses valuation concerns with a reverse DCF [E47], yet ignores that the price-to-book ratio sits at a lofty 5.44x compared to a sector benchmark of just 1.3x [E7]. Finally, insider confidence is visibly waning as promoter holdings have dropped by 8.63 percentage points over recent periods [E41, E63], accompanied by high annualised volatility of 50.5% [E54] that undermines the stability of the bull's technical narrative.

Conceded: [E30], [E64]. While the bear points to a drop in quarterly operating margin [E30] and rising debtor days [E64], the company still generated Rs 12 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 11 Cr in free cash flow for Mar 2026 [E34, E35]. The bear highlights high P/B and falling promoter stakes [E7, E41], but ignores that fundamental earnings power remains exceptional with a ROCE of 26.6% to 30.0% and an ROE up to 25.4% [E10, E12, E13], heavily outperforming sector medians of 11.76% and 9.51% [E9, E10]. Furthermore, the rules-based screen awards the company a high-confidence BUY score of 92 out of 100 backed by tremendous recent momentum including 107% TTM sales growth and 163% TTM profit growth [E17, E21, E65].

Conceded: [E10], [E12], [E13], [E17], [E21]. While exceptional ROCE, ROE, and TTM growth figures are cited, high reported profits are severely disconnected from cash generation, evidenced by a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.46x where operating cash flow is only 54% of operating profit [E33, E36]. Furthermore, debtor days have doubled from 58.4 to 121 days, confirming that the stellar top-line and bottom-line expansions are heavily dependent on uncollected receivables rather than realized cash [E64]. The bull points to strong sector-beating metrics [E9, E10], but ignores that the company trades at a rich price-to-book ratio of 5.44x against a sector benchmark of just 1.3x [E7]. Finally, the high-confidence screen score and momentum arguments [E65] overlook insider divestment, as promoters have steadily reduced their holding by 8.63 percentage points down to 64.24% [E41].
